Reset & Revert

You might say

A shared commit added a debug entry. How can I undo that and keep later work?

Reset moves the current branch and handles changes by mode; revert adds a commit that offsets an earlier change·Suppose B adjusts navigation and C accidentally adds a debug entry. If C is only local, reset can move the branch pointer; --soft keeps changes staged, the default --mixed resets the index but leaves working-tree files, and --hard also replaces tracked working-tree files. If C is on a shared branch and teammates may have based work on it, revert usually appends a commit that offsets C while preserving later history. If later edits overlap with C, revert may also require conflict resolution.
Know first
CommitPush
ResetRevert
git revert a1b2c3d

Local B adjusts navigation, and C accidentally adds a debug entry; shared history later includes teammate D. Reset moves the branch pointer and updates the index or working tree by mode. Revert appends E after D, offsets C, and keeps history. Inspect the commit diffs and working-tree status before choosing.

You can say this to an AI Agent

“

Commit C accidentally added a debug entry, and a teammate later made D. Review the diffs for C and D, then use git revert C to append an offsetting commit. Explain possible conflicts and only resolve the parts related to C. Confirm B’s navigation and D’s content remain, the debug entry is gone, rerun the page, and tell me the new commit hash.

When to use it

  • For an unshared commit, consider reset only after checking staged and working-tree changes
    $ git reset --hard HEAD~1HEAD is now at 3f9c2ab Adjust navigation spacing
  • Keep changes but redo the commit with --soft
    $ git reset --soft HEAD~1Changes stay staged; restage and commit after tidying up
  • For a shared commit, consider revert and check for conflicts
    $ git revert a1b2c3d[main 9e8f7a6] Revert "Add debug code by mistake"
  • Before --hard, inspect tracked-file changes it will replace in the index and working tree
    git status shows uncommitted changesreset --hard discards these changes too

When NOT to use it

  • Reset a shared branch and force push without coordinating with teammates
    Force pushing after resetting a pushed commit splits teammates' copiesDo not rewrite shared history; use revert
  • Run reset --hard without checking which tracked-file changes it will replace
    Two hours of uncommitted work disappear with reset --hardRun git status first to confirm
  • Revert without reviewing later edits that may overlap and need conflict resolution
    Reverted a teammate's commit without telling themThey keep building on reverted work, creating needless conflicts
  • Skip verification after undoing

Reset moves the branch pointer so the commit is no longer in that branch's later history; whether its changes remain depends on the mode. Revert keeps the original commit and adds an offsetting commit.
Variants
--soft
git reset --soft HEAD~1
Undo the commit but keep the changes to restage them
--hard
git reset --hard HEAD~1
Move the branch to the previous commit and replace later tracked-file index and working-tree state; check first
revert
git revert a1b2c3d
Undo a pushed commit without rewriting shared history
Typical use cases
Local commits B and C, including a debug entry
Local main · C has not been shared
a1b2c3d (HEAD → main) Add debug entry by mistake · C 3f9c2ab Adjust navigation spacing · B 81a0b11 Create page
UndoC · debug entry
KeepB · navigation update

Use git log / git show to confirm the target commit and its changes first.

Reset --soft moves the branch but keeps staged changes
git reset --soft HEAD~1
HEAD -> 3f9c2ab Adjust navigation spacing
Branch pointerMoves to B
IndexKeeps C's changes staged
Working filesKeep C's changes

Reset updates the branch, index, and working tree according to its mode. --hard replaces tracked working-tree changes, so check status first.

Revert appends an offsetting commit to shared history
Shared main · teammate D was committed after C
3f9c2ab B · Adjust navigation spacing a1b2c3d C · Add debug entry by mistake 9b8c7d6 D · Teammate updates help copy (HEAD, origin/main)
Offset Cgit revert a1b2c3d
New EAppend Revert C after D

This does not move shared C or the teammate's D. If later edits overlap with C, revert may also require manual conflict resolution.

Recheck navigation and teammate changes remain

BNavigation update remains
COriginal commit stays in history
DTeammate's help copy remains
